question.:question/problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=y\,i-x\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+(1-{t}^{2})\,k$ for $t\in [-1,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,z=1-{t}^{2}.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i-x\,j \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j-2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j-2t\,k) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\cdot \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)+0\cdot (-2t) \\  & =-\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t)-\pi {cos}^{2}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(-\pi )\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\pi [t]_{-1}^{1} \\  & =-\pi (1-(-1)) \\  & =-2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ=\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\mathrm dt.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\cos{\left(\pi t \right)},\quad y=\sin{\left(\pi t \right)},\quad z=1 - t^{2}.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\left(y\right)\,i+\left(- x\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k \\ & =\left(\sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(- \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,i+\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,j+\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(1 - t^{2}\right)\,k \\ & =\left(- \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(\pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(- 2 t\right)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) & =\left(\left(\sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(- \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k\right)\cdot\left(\left(- \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(\pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(- 2 t\right)\,k\right) \\ & =\left(\sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\cdot\left(- \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(- \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\cdot\left(\pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot\left(- 2 t\right) \\ & =\left(- \pi \sin^{2}{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(- \pi \cos^{2}{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =- \pi\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ=\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr & =\int_{-1}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{-1}^{1}\left(- \pi\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[- \pi t\right]_{-1}^{1} \\ & =[\left(- \pi\right)]-[\left(\pi\right)] \\ & =- 2 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=\left(y\right)\,i+\left(x\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,k$ for $t\in [0,2 \pi).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ=\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\mathrm dt.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\sin{\left(t \right)},\quad y=\cos{\left(t \right)},\quad z=2 \sin{\left(t \right)}.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\left(y\right)\,i+\left(x\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k \\ & =\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,j+\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,k \\ & =\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) & =\left(\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k\right)\cdot\left(\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,j+\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,k\right) \\ & =\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ & =\left(\cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =\cos{\left(2 t \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ=\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(\cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\frac{\sin{\left(2 t \right)}}{2}\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =[\left(0\right)]-[\left(0\right)] \\ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=\left(- 2 x + 3 y\right)\,i+\left(0\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\left(3 t^{2} - 3 t\right)\,i+\left(2 t^{3} - 2 t\right)\,j+\left(\sin{\left(2 \pi t \right)}\right)\,k$ for $t\in [0,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ=\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\mathrm dt.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3 t^{2} - 3 t,\quad y=2 t^{3} - 2 t,\quad z=\sin{\left(2 \pi t \right)}.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\left(- 2 x + 3 y\right)\,i+\left(0\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k \\ & =\left(6 t^{3} - 6 t^{2}\right)\,i+\left(0\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(3 t^{2} - 3 t\right)\,i+\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(2 t^{3} - 2 t\right)\,j+\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\sin{\left(2 \pi t \right)}\right)\,k \\ & =\left(6 t - 3\right)\,i+\left(6 t^{2} - 2\right)\,j+\left(2 \pi \cos{\left(2 \pi t \right)}\right)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) & =\left(\left(6 t^{3} - 6 t^{2}\right)\,i+\left(0\right)\,j+\left(0\right)\,k\right)\cdot\left(\left(6 t - 3\right)\,i+\left(6 t^{2} - 2\right)\,j+\left(2 \pi \cos{\left(2 \pi t \right)}\right)\,k\right) \\ & =\left(6 t^{3} - 6 t^{2}\right)\cdot\left(6 t - 3\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot\left(6 t^{2} - 2\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot\left(2 \pi \cos{\left(2 \pi t \right)}\right) \\ & =\left(36 t^{4} - 54 t^{3} + 18 t^{2}\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =\left(6 t - 3\right) \left(6 t^{3} - 6 t^{2}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ=\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr & =\int_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{1}\left(\left(6 t - 3\right) \left(6 t^{3} - 6 t^{2}\right)\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\frac{36 t^{5}}{5} - \frac{27 t^{4}}{2} + 6 t^{3}\right]_{0}^{1} \\ & =[\left(6\right)+\left(- \frac{27}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{36}{5}\right)]-[\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)] \\ & =- \frac{3}{10}\end{aligned}
